title: Riptide - Data Trust

list.name: database
list.label: Database

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT database FROM system.tables WHERE name = 'flows'

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT database FROM system.tables WHERE name = 'flows'

list.name: tenant
list.label: Tenant

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT tenant FROM ${database}.flows ORDER BY tenant

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT tenant FROM ${database}.flows ORDER BY tenant

list.name: zone
list.label: Zone

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT zone FROM ${database}.flows ORDER BY zone

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT zone FROM ${database}.flows ORDER BY zone

panels.title: Distinct sampling configurations

targets.rawSql:
SELECT uniqExact((samplingAlgorithm, samplingInterval)) AS "Configurations"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.description: How many different sampling algorithm and interval combinations are in use across the selected scope. More than one means byte figures from different exporters are not directly comparable — every top-N ranking in the other dashboards silently assumes they are.

panels.title: Flows with a clock correction applied

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(100 * countIf(clockCorrection IS NOT NULL) / nullIf(count(), 0), 2)
       AS "Corrected"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.description: Share of flows whose timestamps riptide had to shift because the exporter's clock disagreed with the collector's beyond the configured threshold. Corrected flows are usable; a high share means an exporter needs NTP, not that the data is wrong.

panels.title: Traffic without an organisation label

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(100 * sumIf(bytes, organisation = '') / nullIf(sum(bytes), 0), 2)
       AS "Unlabelled"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.description: Share of bytes carrying an empty organisation. These flows are invisible to any per-organisation reporting or row policy that filters on it.

panels.title: Exporters reporting

targets.rawSql:
SELECT uniqExact(exporterAddr) AS "Exporters"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.description: Distinct exporter addresses seen in the range. Compare against your inventory: this dashboard describes the data you have, not the data you expected.

panels.title: Sampling by exporter

targets.rawSql:
SELECT if(exporterName != '', exporterName, exporterAddr) AS "Exporter",
       toString(samplingAlgorithm) AS "Algorithm",
       samplingInterval AS "Interval", count() AS "Flows",
       sum(bytes) AS "Bytes"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY "Exporter", "Algorithm", "Interval"
ORDER BY "Flows" DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description: The sampling algorithm and interval each exporter reported, with how much traffic it contributed. An interval of 1 is unsampled. Two exporters with different intervals contribute bytes on different scales — this table is where you find that out before it distorts a comparison.

panels.title: Clock correction by exporter

targets.rawSql:
SELECT if(exporterName != '', exporterName, exporterAddr) AS "Exporter",
       countIf(clockCorrection IS NOT NULL) AS "Corrected flows",
       round(100 * countIf(clockCorrection IS NOT NULL) / nullIf(count(), 0), 2)
         AS "Share",
       min(clockCorrection) AS "Min correction",
       median(clockCorrection) AS "Median correction",
       max(clockCorrection) AS "Max correction"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY "Exporter" HAVING "Corrected flows" > 0
ORDER BY "Corrected flows" DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description: Which exporters needed their timestamps shifted, how often, and by how much. The magnitude is the raw stored correction value, shown for comparison between exporters rather than as an absolute duration. A single exporter dominating this table is an NTP problem on that device.

panels.title: Scope matrix — tenant, organisation, zone

targets.rawSql:
SELECT tenant AS "Tenant",
       if(organisation = '', '(unset)', organisation) AS "Organisation",
       if(zone = '', '(unset)', zone) AS "Zone",
       uniqExact(exporterAddr) AS "Exporters", count() AS "Flows",
       sum(bytes) AS "Bytes"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY "Tenant", "Organisation", "Zone"
ORDER BY "Bytes" DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description: How traffic divides across the multi-tenant dimensions. Empty cells are flows that arrived without that label. This is the view that shows whether onboarding actually tagged everything it was supposed to.

panels.title: Exporter identity

targets.rawSql:
SELECT exporterAddr AS "Address",
       if(exporterName != '', exporterName, '(unnamed)') AS "Name",
       if(system != '', system, '(unset)') AS "System",
       toString(flowProtocol) AS "Protocol",
       engineType AS "Engine type", engineId AS "Engine ID",
       max(receivedAt) AS "Last seen", count() AS "Flows"
FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY "Address", "Name", "System", "Protocol", "Engine type", "Engine ID"
ORDER BY "Flows" DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description: Each exporter with the protocol version, engine identifiers and system name it presented. A device appearing twice with different engine IDs has been renumbered or replaced — which breaks any history keyed on that identity.

description: Can the other dashboards be believed? Sampling configuration, clock corrections, scope labelling and exporter identity — the metadata that silently invalidates a byte comparison when it changes. Read this one first when a number looks wrong somewhere else. Collection Health answers whether data is arriving; this answers whether it means what you think.
